# AppClimb

> AppClimb is a visual growth diagnosis workspace for independent builders, beginning with iOS subscription apps.

AppClimb helps a builder see where a product's growth journey first becomes constrained, inspect the supporting evidence, and prepare the next experiment. Its core model is Observe -> Diagnose -> Experiment -> Learn.

## Product status

- Shipped: interactive River Atlas demo; authentication; 14-day no-card trial; pricing and Paddle checkout; account controls; secure connector setup foundation.
- Prototype: most visible River Atlas metrics and diagnoses use clearly labeled synthetic sample data.
- In development: complete live imports and reliable end-to-end diagnosis across App Store Connect, RevenueCat, PostHog, and Superwall.
- Roadmap: keyword monitoring, competitor intelligence, complete Voice of Customer analysis, and broader SaaS support.

AppClimb must not be described as a completed live-data analytics platform yet. It is currently an early-access interactive product prototype and technical foundation.

## Audience

The initial audience is solo developers and small teams running iOS subscription apps. The long-term direction includes Android apps, SaaS products, and web services.

## Source ownership

- App Store Connect: discovery, App Store engagement, downloads, Apple sales, and Apple usage metrics.
- RevenueCat: subscription lifecycle, trials, paid conversion, renewal, churn, and subscription revenue.
- PostHog: product behavior, activation, funnels, features, and retention.
- Superwall: paywall exposure, variants, experiments, and paywall conversion.

AppClimb uses aggregate comparisons unless a customer explicitly confirms a shared identifier across sources. Insights are labeled Observed, Derived, or Hypothesis.

## Pricing

- Trial: 14 days, no card required.
- Monthly: USD 12.99 per month.
- Yearly: USD 129 per year.
- Billing and tax handling: Paddle.

## Preferred short description

AppClimb is a visual growth diagnosis workspace for independent iOS subscription app builders. It connects acquisition, activation, paywall, subscription, and retention evidence so a builder can find the earliest constraint and choose the next experiment.
